Implementation:

- Reconstructed the first conservative stock-like consuming boundary at
  Airoha QDMA RX reason `0x16`, before `eth_type_trans()`. The existing

- Added built-in boolean parameter `stock_wifi_fasttx_consume`. Its BSS-backed
  zero default leaves the new path dormant after every boot.

  unicast plain IPv4/IPv6 frames with exact stock classification, matching

  RX metadata, and calls `dev_queue_xmit()` exactly once. There is no fallback
  after qdisc ownership transfer. Every decline follows exactly one normal

  retain page-pool ownership.

  counters. Direct ndo, scatter, VLAN, multicast, MVAL header policy, vendor
  soft-ratelimit/RPS, dedicated host-adapter rings, and broader ping-pong

Stock finding:

- Stock `hw_nat.ko` installs `PpeWifiFastTxHandler` into exported kernel pointer
  `ra_sw_nat_to_wifi_fast_tx`; stock `qdma_lan.ko` calls it for QDMA CPU reason
  `0x16` before `eth_type_trans()` and returns immediately when the hook takes
  ownership.
- This places a consuming stock FastTX handoff at Ethernet QDMA RX, before
  mt76 token, DMA, TXWI, and TXFREE ownership. The disabled post-token mt76
  FastTX/ping-pong experiments are therefore at the wrong ownership layer.

Implementation:

- Added a non-consuming QDMA reason-`0x16` observer. For a valid FOE hash it
  invokes the existing read-only stock classifier with protocol tag `0x7274`,
  then preserves the normal GRO path. It does not mutate, redirect, queue,
  consume, transmit, or free the SKB.
- Reduced the helper's public custom mt76 interface to the only compiled
  parameter, `npu_stock_copy_mode`. Applying policy scrubs retired module
  arguments while preserving unrelated arguments and avoids same-file shell
  redirection truncation.
- Removed retired mt76 ownership controls from LuCI's declared keys, rendered
  inputs, policy refresh, and save jobs. Stock hostadpt/FastTX/ping-pong/RRO/
  token evidence remains available as read-only diagnostics. Supported
  mt7996e policy controls remain available.

Artifacts:

- Report: `work\W1700K_DEAD_WM_RAW_BAR_RESET_V625_REPORT_20260717.md`, SHA256 `70db110824e2aad002adf83193dacf5bc4af30ed0db3379e37b4e87dee1c21f5`
- Image: `work\w1700k-raw-bar-wfsys-v6.25-20260717-sysupgrade.itb`
- Image SHA256: `6bc32205e00ace586acc59696061ae65a190c639587cb14877c0fe2d3ee99f72`
- Patch: `work\patches\9999zzzp-mt7996-address-stock-wfsys-pulse-through-bar0.patch`
- Patch SHA256: `3f5110ef1e5e7e3ac66db97a974f2a7606d0267cdd484fd32e791bb90711b41f`
- Checked 99-entry bundle: `C:\Users\captain\Downloads\FW\MessingWstuff\FinalResult\Experimental\NpuRawBarResetV625-20260717-UNFLASHED`
- Bundle checksum-set SHA256: `bb6923ac2b0d277713141f431cf68344b8a12f7e97bfa2127927d6ee94cb7fa8`
- Bundle manifest SHA256: `0543c351b5ed3099d997e645a3f68c7f8a0136ee7017e170f4b581f8b8e16429`

Stock finding:

- Full Ghidra analysis closes the action-5 callback chain:
  `mtk_ge_hw_reset()` uses chip-ops slot `+0x28`; MT7990 callback
  `FUN_00100160` toggles argument `0x1f8600`; PCI callback
  `FUN_001005c0` stores to `BAR0 + (offset & 0xffffffff)`.
- The existing local `mt76_wr(0x1f8600)` implementation was not equivalent.
  On the W1700K's MT7996 map it used L2 BAR window `0x1600` with remap value
  `0x1f8`, instead of a literal `BAR0 + 0x1f8600` write.

Implementation:

- Added a dedicated helper that uses the saved original bus write operation
  for `1 -> 1000..1100 us delay -> 0` at raw BAR0 offset `0x1f8600`.
- W1700K prepared/diagnostic recovery and MT7990 full reset use the helper.
  Ordinary MT7996 subsystem reset remains unchanged.
- No stock kernel module or stock userspace binary is included.

Verification:

- Strict checkpatch, clean mt76 prepare/compile, full image build, and zero-new-
  warning comparison against V6.24 pass.
- Address fixture, prepared-source audit, exact machine-code checks, FIT/rootfs
  extraction, module/package identity, firmware/package inventory, and
  forbidden-stock-binary scan pass.
- Full Ghidra analysis recovered 610 functions from the exact unstripped
  `mt7996e.ko`, SHA256
  `36615647286a66267d2e707ccbe653b5a196678a61895671f396c9c8e52048ee`.
- Ghidra proves both raw bus calls, the delay, both reset call sites, and the
  separate remap path inside `mt7996_wr()`.
- V6.24 TXFREE/RRO checks were rerun unchanged and labeled inherited.

Boundary:

- Offline verified and unflashed. Serial access is deferred until tomorrow.
- This corrects the address path but does not yet prove that a dead WM enters
  firmware-download state or recovers on hardware.
- Tomorrow begins with V6.15 mode-0 recovery/baseline gates, then V6.25 mode-0,
  followed by one bounded mode-3/dead-WM serial test.
- Dead-WM/fatal-download recovery remains in progress. FastTX/ping-pong packet
  fate remains the next separate offline phase.

## Status Key

- `REFERENCE-IMAGE`: present in the latest completed FinalResult image.
- `SOURCE-COMPILED`: patched in source and passed targeted compile, but no completed full sysupgrade image is recorded yet.
- `DONE`: implemented and built at least once in the custom image line.
- `PARTIAL`: safe subset, reconstruction, guarded path, or not fully proven equivalent.
- `TELEMETRY`: classified or logged only. It should not own packet fate.
- `LEFT`: not implemented or not proven.

- vendor `wapp`

Current method: reconstruct behavior in OpenWrt patches and expose enough telemetry to know when we are lying to ourselves. Innovation, sadly.

## What Is Left Exactly

### 1. Full `mtk_pci.ko` queue publication equivalence

Still missing or not proven:

- exact PCIe TX queue selection and option-type validation
- physical TX queue base publication equivalence under load
- all TX buffer-space mailbox values and failure handling equivalence
- NPU-visible TX register/base mapping equivalence
- RX event/TXDONE ring ownership semantics
- RX data queue type `6/7` storage and ownership equivalence
- true stock-equivalent `glb_npu_trans1/trans2` global pointer behavior
- true stock-equivalent hostadpt hook ownership

### 2. Full hostadpt RX ownership

Still missing:

- `pci_dma_rx_process_hostadpt()` equivalence
- `pci_dma_rx_poll_hostadpt_ring0()` equivalence
- `_fromHostadptPktHandle_hook` equivalent handoff
- exact RXDONE interrupt disable/poll/re-enable loop is now in the reference image with per-ring owner state and NPU poll-completion re-enable, but it is not yet live-validated under traffic
- returned SKBs handed into WiFi RX exactly like stock

Current boundary: schedule-prep, complete-done-zero, RX process-loop split,
RX owner-clear, scatter-buffer reuse, and corrected `data:+0x08` Type-5
observability are present. The old `info:+0x04` Type-5 CB seed/projection claim
is superseded and those mutations remain inactive. Packet fate stays with
OpenWrt/mt76.

### 2b. Full hostadpt TX ownership

Still missing:

- byte-equivalent `_toHostadptPktHandle_hook()` TX enqueue ownership
- hostadpt-owned SKB lifetime
- exact HWIFI token release and completion ordering
- final switch from mt76 TX completion to hostadpt descriptor SKB-latch ownership
- stress proof under 5 GHz 80 MHz, 5 GHz 160 MHz, MLO, non-MLO, client-client, and routed traffic

Current boundary: TX descriptor publish, immediate doorbell publish, TX descriptor reclaim, toHostadpt hook decision state, opt-in SKB ownership mode, and enqueue failure-path accounting are logged or implemented per stock group.
Opt-in boundary: `npu_stock_hostadpt_tx_skb_ownership=1` now moves SKB freeing to hostadpt descriptor cleanup while leaving token/TXWI release with firmware TXFREE. This still needs live stress proof before becoming default.
Failure boundary: failed hostadpt enqueue is recorded as normal OpenWrt TX status/free cleanup, matching the stock outcome without adding a second free inside `mt76_npu_dma_add_buf()`.

### 3. Full ping-pong packet fate

Still missing:

- true `GET_HIR()==10` mapping
- original-skb source-port-0 mode-2 `netif_rx()` ownership
- L2TP checks
- speed-test checks
- ECNT hook state
- actual branch side effects and final DstPort actions for every VirIfIdx family
- original-skb consume/redirect/drop decision parity

Current boundary: stock VirIfIdx branch classification, DstPort normalization, expected branch-fate side-effect classification, telemetry/classification, plus default-off copied-skb DstPort, `br-lan` FDB bridge, mode-2 source-port-5 `dst_output`, copied-skb source-port-0 `netif_rx`, and original-skb source-port-0 `netif_rx` handoffs for proven subsets. The bridge and source-port-5 handoffs still copy rather than transfer the original skb. The bridge handoff enforces explicit `_left_to_right_test_mode==1`; the source-port-5 handoff uses explicit mode `2`, current-kernel `dst_output(dev_net(dst->dev), skb->sk, skb)`, and `dst->dev` rather than the exact stock `DstPort._1808_8_` global. The source-port-0 original handoff uses current-kernel `DstPort[0xe2]` and current-kernel L2 classification with explicit consumed-SKB ownership rather than direct stock `sk_buff` field writes. L2TP, speed-test, ECNT, TSO callback, black-IP, final DstPort side effects, `GET_HIR()==10`, and full byte-equivalent consume/redirect/drop behavior remain unresolved.

### 4. Full FastTX equivalence

Still missing:

- byte-equivalent DstPort/static-rule/RPS internals
- full ECNT static-rule side effects
- every vendor failure/consume branch
- proof under 5 GHz 80 MHz, 5 GHz 160 MHz, MLO, non-MLO, client-client, and routed traffic

### 5. Full TXFREE/token equivalence

Still missing:

- complete vendor token table model
- exact callback/completion ordering in every error path
- every v0/v1/v4/v5 free-notify edge case
- proof that token leak counters match expected behavior under stress

### 6. Full RRO equivalence

Still missing:

- complete RRO indication command queue model
- all prelink/address-element update paths
- all stop/start sequencing corner cases
- token free-pool start/end, free-pool-full semantics, and addition-read/max-read equivalence
- proof of stock-equivalent BA behavior across MLO links

### 7. Advanced WiFi 7/MLO controls

Still not confidently exposed as user toggles:

- STR-MLMR
- EMLMR
- SRS
- dynamic reconfiguration
- TID-to-link mapping controls
- AFC/standard-power 6 GHz behavior

### 8. Stock userspace WiFi services

Not cloned:

- vendor `wapp`
- vendor `mapd`
- vendor hostapd/wpad behavior
- vendor cloud/provisioning scripts

Reason: they are not needed yet, and dragging vendor userspace into OpenWrt would create a circus with ABI knives.

## 2026-06-29 23:45 +03:00 - Stock TXFREE Unmap Semantics Audit

- Report: `work\W1700K_STOCK_TXFREE_UNMAP_SEMANTICS_AUDIT_20260629.md`
- Ghidra proof output: `work\ghidra-mtk-hwifi-unmap-path-20260629.txt`
- Image produced: none.
- Patch produced: none.

Finding:

- Stock `mtk_tk_unmap_tx_q()` calls its per-token queue-operation unmap callback only after a token entry is available.
- Current OpenWrt NPU host-adapter TX already preserves the important ownership split: `mt7996_tx_prepare_skb()` marks the descriptor-side payload buffer `skip_unmap`, `mt76_npu_dma_add_buf()` mirrors that into `entry->npu_dma_skip`, and `mt7996_txwi_free()` calls `mt76_connac_txp_skb_unmap()` from the TXFREE token path after token claim.
- Descriptor reclaim therefore skips the descriptor-side payload DMA unmap while TXFREE owns the payload unmap, avoiding a double-unmap.

Decision:

- No behavior patch was applied because the current path is already behavior-aligned for payload DMA ownership.
- Keep this as behavior-level parity only; exact stock helper byte parity and all free-notify error paths remain open.

## 2026-06-30 01:41 +03:00 - Stock TXFREE Unmap/TXQ Edge Audit

- Report: `work\W1700K_STOCK_TXFREE_UNMAP_TXQ_AUDIT_20260630.md`
- Ghidra proof output: `work\ghidra-mtk-hwifi-token-helpers-20260629.txt`
- Image produced: none.
- Patch produced: none.
- Latest flashable image remains: `C:\Users\captain\Downloads\FW\MessingWstuff\FinalResult\w1700k-stock-txfree-release-error-20260630-sysupgrade.itb`

Finding:

- Stock `mtk_tk_unmap_tx_q()` returns `-EINVAL` only when called with a NULL token entry. After a valid token claim, the helper calls the callback at `param_1 + 0x640` when present, but ignores that callback return and still returns `0`.
- Stock `mtk_tk_get_tx_q()` returns `token_entry + 0x10`, so TXQ NULL after a non-NULL `mtk_tk_get_entry()` result is structurally unreachable in the decompiled path.
- Current OpenWrt rejects missing/out-of-range/duplicate/not-ready tokens before TXWI/SKB side effects, then uses deferred finish quarantine for post-claim ownership failures.

Decision:

- No behavior patch was applied.
- Closed: unmap callback failure propagation and TXQ-NULL-after-valid-token do not need synthetic OpenWrt behavior.
- Still open: byte-identical stock token-entry memory layout, complete `_fromHostadptPktHandle_hook()` parity, ping-pong packet fate, RRO equivalence, and live stress proof.

  word `+4` as the Type-5 source. Exact stock hostadpt/PCI analysis proves the
  projector consumes descriptor `data:+0x08`; `info:+0x04` is separate PPE/
  count/reason metadata.
- Current OpenWrt already models the provider boundary, RXINFO handoff/cache, scatter failure classes, type-5 metadata projection, RX CB seed, type-5 bus-fate classify/guarded consume, and CPU-index writeback.

Decision:

- No behavior patch was applied.
- Do not write stock offsets `0x38/0x40` into the current `skb->cb` layout until live mt76 RX-status correlation proves the mapping is safe.

## 2026-07-04 20:19 +03:00 - Stock Hostadpt Ring Lifecycle Source Gate

Artifacts:

- Report: `work\W1700K_STOCK_HOSTADPT_RING_LIFECYCLE_SOURCE_GATE_20260704.md`
- Report SHA256: `a61e47af39982277a33bc8df0a43271524d6715319063eb71242fee7e63d21c7`

Evidence:

- Stock `hostadpt.ko` uses two RX rings of `0x200` descriptors with `0x18` stride, at NPU hostadpt registers `0x180/0x184/0x188/0x18c` and `0x190/0x194/0x198/0x19c`.
- Stock `hostadpt.ko` uses two TX rings of `0x400` descriptors with `0xd0` stride, at NPU hostadpt registers `0xa0/0xa4/0xa8/0xac` and `0xb0/0xb4/0xb8/0xbc`.
- Stock TX enqueue only publishes a descriptor when owner bit 0 is clear and the NPU readback/free-space distance is greater than `5`; the descriptor owner bit is set last.
- Stock TX reclaim walks from software CPU index to NPU readback index, unmaps the payload DMA mapping, frees the skb pointer stored at descriptor offset `+8`, clears owner bit, and advances the CPU index.
- Stock `npu_pci_dma_tx_data_queue()` calls `_ra_sw_nat_hook_tx()` with opcode `0x7274`; return `0` releases the token and consumes the skb, while non-zero takes a `0x4c` descriptor snapshot and calls `_toHostadptPktHandle_hook()`.
- Stock RX completion replaces the DMA buffer with `skbmgr_alloc_skb4k()`, advances replacement skb data by `0x40`, maps `0xdac`, updates `0x18c` or `0x19c`, and calls `_ra_sw_nat_hook_rxinfo()` with opcode `0x7275` when available.
- Stock `mtk_hwifi.ko` selector fate counters map to `rx_cnt`, `rx_legacy_drop_cnt`, `rx_pn_check_drop_cnt`, and `rx_incmd_reason_drop_cnt` at offsets `+0x94/+0x9c/+0xa0/+0xa4`.

## 2026-07-05 - Static Stock Updater Audit

Artifacts:

- Report: `work\W1700K_STATIC_STOCK_UPDATER_AUDIT_20260705.md`

Implemented:

- Audited the extracted stock rootfs upgrade path without touching any live router.
- Compared extracted lighttpd/Axon routing against the wrong-target `192.168.1.1` web evidence.
- Inspected stock `/sbin/sysupgrade`, `/lib/upgrade/platform.sh`, `/lib/upgrade/nand.sh`, `secureupgrade.ko`, `libblapi_system.so`, `gcontrol.sh`, and `rma.sh`.

Findings:

- The extracted W1700K stock rootfs uses Axon/lighttpd FastCGI through `/tmp/fcgi` and `/cgi/...` routes.
- No static rootfs evidence was found for `upgrade_web_app.cgi`, `login_web_app.cgi`, or `wlan_config_web_app.cgi`; this reinforces that the earlier `192.168.1.1` live web surface was the wrong target.
- Stock `platform_check_image()` accepts only magic `32524448` or `48445232`, with optional secure header offset from `/userfs/bin/blapi_cmd system check_secure_tclinux`.
- Stock `platform_do_upgrade()` writes by `mtd write` to `firmware`, `tclinux`, or `tclinux_slave`, then updates `fwupd_type`/`fwupd_state`.
- `/lib/upgrade/nand.sh` exists but this platform script does not call `nand_do_platform_check` or `nand_do_upgrade`.
- `secureupgrade.ko` and `libblapi_system.so` expose secure stock-image validation/upgrade plumbing.
- Factory helpers expect stock artifacts such as `tcboot.bin`, `tclinux.bin`, or stock compressed firmware bundles.

Verdict:

- Do not use a stock web/sysupgrade path for the current custom OpenWrt sysupgrade ITB unless a separate verified W1700K-specific updater implementation proves image acceptance and intended NAND/UBI writes.

Boundary:

- Static audit only.
- No source datapath changes, image rebuild, network probing, flash, or router config change.

- Headless Ghidra call-neighborhood analysis traced the stock vendor TX path
  from `mtk_ge_tx_data` through `npu_pci_dma_tx_data_queue`, token detachment,
  `_toHostadptPktHandle_hook`, and the dedicated host-adapter TX rings.
- Stock detaches the vendor token entry before hostadpt handoff, stores the SKB
  and payload DMA ownership in the host-adapter descriptor, and reclaims/unmaps/
  frees from the firmware consumer index.
- OpenWrt's NPU firmware contains the corresponding `0xd0`-stride host-adapter
  polling path and copies the same `0x4c` TX metadata into internal descriptors.
- Current mt76 instead uses split ownership: descriptor lifetime follows the NPU
  consumer index, while payload/SKB/TXWI lifetime remains in the host token IDR
  until TXFREE. This is a plausible mode-3 boundary, not yet a proven defect.
- The next patch is therefore a bounded, non-mutating consumer-versus-TXFREE
  ordering probe. No ownership behavior will change before live ordering data.

Performance evidence:

- The user again reported saturating the gigabit Ethernet connection on the
  current mode-0 control. This confirms the general radio/OpenWrt datapath is
  not capped at the older 13-35 MB/s observations.
- Mode-3 eligible-unicast throughput remains unproven and is the decisive live
  gate. Router-local traffic is not a substitute because it can bypass the NPU
  forwarding path.

  18 later TXFREE events, and one outstanding token. Invalid, untracked,
  duplicate, and mismatch counters were zero.

Reverse-engineering decision:

- Stock `mtk_hwifi.ko` requests tokens from the free-list head and appends
  released tokens at the tail, producing FIFO/round-robin reuse.
- Stock `mtk_pci.ko` detaches the token before host-adapter handoff. Current
  mt76 can immediately reuse a low released ID through `idr_alloc()`.
- Therefore no early consumer-owned token release is being implemented yet. A
  late old TXFREE could otherwise target a newly reused OpenWrt token.
- The next phase closes stock/OpenWrt late-TXFREE and token-reuse semantics,
  then runs the controlled eligible-unicast mode-0/mode-3 throughput gate.

ETA:

- Token-reuse decision: `0.5-1.5 focused days`.

- Stock Ghidra report SHA256:
  `b184835986e266bf21f352231a9ebca37cce002cb3452550139540f09a13ede7`.
- Stock fingerprints SHA256:
  `d65f34ed91884de8e3c678dc2dc8704e4aa1d54db23a8ec0cc0eb7571c3143ba`.
- OpenWrt fingerprints SHA256:
  `198b6d001f1787bd4116b0cd6ab990a26088e71041c323294fddcdf7210b201b`.

  `d81b4076c3d8952cb738f0211cbbe90302d422e5c414e3d9e8f7c23412420337`.
- Ghidra project: `work\ghidra-projects\W1700K_NPU_FW_STOCK_20260711`.

Finding:

- `248/258` stock functions have exact normalized-shape OpenWrt matches.
- Stock hostadpt enqueue allocates an NPU-local token, copies payload into a
  0x800-byte local buffer, copies 0x4c bytes of TX metadata, and publishes the
  local token. OpenWrt forwards the host DMA address and copied host token.
- Stock and OpenWrt token allocators are FIFO, while current host mt76 token
  allocation may immediately reuse a released low ID.
- OpenWrt reserves disjoint token namespaces with host token start 8192. A
  guarded copy/remap path can therefore classify low TXFREE IDs as NPU-local
  status and complete the original high host token at consumer advance.
- Existing OpenWrt NPU mode linearizes the SKB. The nearby nonlinear-SKB TODO
  is stale and is not being treated as the present defect.

Decision and roadmap:

- Build v28 as a default-off stock-copy/remap experiment. Keep the direct path
  intact, mark only eligible packets of at most 2048 bytes, and make the host
  ownership change atomic with the firmware remap.
- Do not release host tokens early on the existing direct firmware path.
- Roadmap: `work\W1700K_NPU_ROADMAP_ETA_V28_STOCK_COPY_20260711.md`.
- Roadmap SHA256:
  `411aaf960ca628b03109125ea52895da0c0d517f25e856d750824b39d98976d8`.
- Best-case production candidate ETA: `2-3 focused working days`.
- One additional causal correction: `4-6 focused days total`.
- Multiple boundaries: `7-12 focused days total`.
- Exhaustive stock-path parity: add `10-20 focused days`.

State boundary:

## 2026-07-12 17:20 +03:00 - Live Gigabit Mode-3 Capture

Evidence and decision:

  EHT160 client on physical radio 2 with 2161/2402 Mbit/s negotiated rates.

  bound/WLAN entries, so the observed path used direct mt76 WLAN-NPU transport
  rather than a bound PPE flow.

  enqueue/consumer/TXFREE accounting, allocation balance equaled current
  ownership, and all invalid/missing/duplicate/mismatch counters were zero.

  zero ownership, queue, token-release, RRO, or netdev risk deltas.
- Conclusion: direct mode 3 is not the demonstrated 1 GbE bottleneck;
  stock-copy remains disabled pending evidence of a benefit beyond that
  ceiling.

Stock analysis and implementation:

- Ghidra/decompile review confirmed stock hostadpt maps one
  `skb->data`/`skb->len` DMA span and masks length into a 13-bit descriptor
  without an explicit upper-length or nonlinear-SKB guard.
- v31 preserves the single-span contract but removes unsafe truncation:
  nonlinear NPU TX SKBs are linearized and lengths above 8191 are rejected
  before payload DMA mapping or mt7996 token allocation.
- Publication is also rejected before mapping when the current descriptor
  still owns its DONE bit.
- Passive shape/GSO/linearization/oversize/busy counters and last-shape state
  are exposed in `w1700k-stock-npu-parity-map`.

## 2026-07-12 19:40 +03:00 - Memory and LuCI Lockup Diagnosis

  1,867,960 KiB. BusyBox reported only 169,352 KiB used, `/tmp` used about
  3 MiB, and there was no OOM or storage-pressure evidence.

  seconds. MCU command `0x00130022` is `GET_MIB_INFO`; AER could not recover

## 2026-07-13 - Stock Descriptor Bit 31 Completion Claim Rejected

- Resolved the stock RV32 descriptor-worker calling convention at instruction
  level. `FUN_ram_840081f6` passes the current `0xd0` descriptor in `a1`
  to `FUN_ram_84004aca`.
- The worker extracts payload length with `(word0 << 1) >> 19`, which uses
  bits 18 through 30 and explicitly discards bit 31. Neither function writes
  bit 31 before advancing the NPU consumer index.
- The existing guarded stock-copy experiment incorrectly treated its own
  host-set bit 31 as a firmware completion acknowledgment.
- Added
  `9999zc-mt76-quarantine-host-owned-npu-sched-bit.patch`. It fail-closes
  `npu_stock_copy_mode`, blocks consumer-side token completion from bit 31,
  and adds read-only observed/changed counters.
- `checkpatch.pl`, clean prepare, and clean mt76 compile with
  `W1700K_EXPERIMENTAL_MT76_NPU=1` pass. Built-module strings and function
  disassembly confirm the completion callback is absent from the path.
- No full image was built or flashed. Report:
  `work\W1700K_NPU_DESCRIPTOR_BIT31_QUARANTINE_20260713.md`.

## 2026-07-13 - Native And Custom NPU Copy Contracts Separated

- Hash and size comparison proves native stock and Linux-firmware NPU blobs
  are different for both RV32 code and data.
- Ghidra normalized fingerprints match `170/258` stock functions exactly, but
  the host-adapter payload ownership path differs materially.
- Stock copies payload and metadata into an allocated local token buffer;
  untouched Linux-firmware keeps the host payload DMA address and copies only
  metadata.

  does not acknowledge bit 31, while the packaged custom OpenWrt trampoline
  deliberately preserves it on success and clears it on fallback.

  `9999zc-mt76-validate-custom-npu-copy-remap.patch`. Host-token completion now
  additionally requires the descriptor payload address to change from the
  original host DMA address into the `0x80000000` NPU-local alias.
- Native stock or an unpatched OpenWrt blob therefore fails closed to ordinary
  TXFREE ownership.
- Strict checkpatch, clean NPU-enabled prepare, mt76 compile, module strings,
  and AArch64 disassembly gates pass.
- No full image was built or flashed. Stock-copy/remap remains default-off and
  requires a fresh controlled live validation.

  only when ownership is reported as zero. Real unregister therefore cannot

## 2026-08-05 - cfg80211 ABI Root Cause And V6.31 Image Gate

  976. `CONFIG_NETPOLL` inserts `netpoll_info *npinfo` immediately before that
  field. Kernel-built probes prove 976 without NETPOLL and 984 with NETPOLL.

  functions. The shipped cfg80211 therefore uses the wrong layout by eight
  bytes, explaining the notifier-registration spinlock fault.

  and
  `57e41f27f12be1a6e9691fa0892c053bc13727e8ab7c8af349dd5f58d271426e`.

Implementation and evidence:

- The NPU TX ring is coherent DMA memory. The old publication boundary used
  CPU-only `smp_wmb()` before DONE and had no explicit DMA acquire before
  reading returned descriptor state. This could expose DONE to the NPU while
  TXWI, address, or SKB-shadow fields were stale, or expose stale CTRL/ADDR to
  the CPU after completion.
- Added patch
  `work\patches\9999zzzzzzzf-mt76-fix-npu-tx-descriptor-publication.patch`,
  SHA256
  `03770cb972d0c8077f8e4243c0ca65635134b162537d7bf01b2c6f8e7bf2b2d3`.
  It uses `dma_wmb()` before `WRITE_ONCE(DONE)`, pairs `dma_rmb()` with
  completion reads, snapshots CTRL/ADDR with `READ_ONCE()`, and recycles DONE
  with `WRITE_ONCE()`.
- Ordering verifier SHA256
  `6f993374833dacc68fccf67d57dc2a9e2a6412c691d19e788c2482a523e2582a`
  reports `PASS_V638_NPU_DESCRIPTOR_ORDERING checks=28`. The state-space model
  reproduces seven old producer stale states and three old completion stale
  states; the corrected model admits none.
- Strict checkpatch has 0 errors, 0 warnings, and 0 checks. Clean prepare,

## V6.48 mt7996 PCIe AER Recovery and Guarded Flash - 2026-08-06

- Root-caused the recurring WiFi/LuCI lockup to a PCIe completion timeout
  followed by Linux AER permanently disconnecting mt7996 because neither the
  primary nor HIF2 PCI driver registered an `error_detected` callback. The
  stock kernel avoids this path because `CONFIG_PCIEPORTBUS` is disabled,
  while the OpenWrt kernel enables `CONFIG_PCIEPORTBUS=y` and
  `CONFIG_PCIEAER=y`.
- Added `9999zzzzzzzzo-mt7996-handle-nonfatal-pcie-aer.patch`, SHA256
  `8f5dc98cba54e4fc10e08cd733a73ea4948e95a3e1215e4c07b064b964793e36`.

  completion-ownership gap: unregister reached `mt7996_tx_token_put()` before
  disabling the IRQ tasklet and without draining RX/TX NAPI. A scheduled
  TXFREE consumer could therefore claim a token while unregister removed the
  IDR entry, cleared claim ownership, and freed the TXWI.

## Stock RV32 TXFREE Identity Closure - 2026-09-01 15:20 +03:00

- Read-only full-image Ghidra 12.1.2 analysis recovered and exported 305/305
  functions from the hash-gated stock RV32 image. Independent GNU disassembly
  agrees with Ghidra on all six direct token-release and four token-allocation
  sites. All package hashes and 25 final validation checks reverify locally.
- Normal stock TXFREE strips each completion to a raw 15-bit ID and appends it
  to a 16-bit circular FIFO. Normal release/allocation has no generation,
  epoch, descriptor/ring identity, retired-state lookup, duplicate scan, or
  fixed quarantine. FIFO rotation delays reuse but does not make identity safe;
  a duplicate completion can enqueue and later allocate the same token twice.
- The stock stop protocol acknowledges selected worker shutdown, not TXFREE
  drain. It leaves the TXFREE worker enabled through its readiness flag and has
  no recovered producer/consumer equality wait, queue-empty acknowledgment,
  completion-epoch bump, or residual partial-CIDX flush.
- Report:
  `work/analysis/stock-rv32-txfree-deep-20260901/REPORT.md`, SHA256
  `5f6a5009143388d9c7a611e60b5a094b79cbcdc274d6ec689ff6e03ee0cbbf6`.
